      "title": "High frequency of vital signs and lab tests at weekly visits",
      "quote": "Vital Signsh | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every visit including all weekly visits, which is burdensome for patients and sites, especially when combined with frequent lab tests.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital sign collection to visits where dosing or key assessments occur, or allow patient-reported vitals at home for stable patients."
    },
    {
      "title": "Clinical lab tests at every weekly visit",
      "quote": "Clinical Laboratory Tests (hematology, serum chemistry, urinalysis)l | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Hematology, chemistry, and urinalysis are required at every weekly visit, which is a high burden for patients and may be unnecessary for safety monitoring.",
      "fix": "Reduce lab frequency to every other week or align with key safety assessments (e.g., before each cycle)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor biopsy at screening and W5D1 may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor Biopsyq | X |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Tumor biopsies are invasive and may be challenging to obtain at both screening and W5D1, especially if the tumor is not easily accessible. This could lead to missing data.",
      "fix": "Consider making the on-treatment biopsy optional or allowing archival tissue if fresh biopsy is not feasible."
    },
    {
      "title": "Pharmacokinetic sampling at multiple visits including W5D1 and W6D1",
      "quote": "Pharmacokinetic Samplingn |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK sampling at W5D1, W6D1, and W6D2 may be burdensome and could be consolidated to fewer visits without losing critical data.",
      "fix": "Evaluate if PK samples at W5D1 and W6D1 can be combined or reduced to a single timepoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight windows for weekly visits (±2 days) may be hard to meet",
      "quote": "W2D1 ± 2d 2 (Day 8) | W3D1 ± 2d 3 (Day 15) | W4D1 ± 2d 4 2 (Day 22) | W5D1 ±2d 5 (Day 29) | W6D1 ±2d 6 (Day 36)",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "A ±2-day window for weekly visits is tight and may be difficult for patients to adhere to, especially if they have travel or work constraints.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the window to ±3 days for weekly visits to improve feasibility."
    },
    {
      "title": "Disease assessment (radiographic imaging) at screening and EOT only",
      "quote": "Disease Assessment (radiographic imaging)r | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  | X |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Radiographic imaging is only at screening and EOT, with no interim tumor assessment. This may not adequately capture response or progression during treatment.",
      "fix": "Add an interim disease assessment (e.g., at W7D1 or Q3W) to monitor treatment response."
    },
    {
      "title": "Autoimmune laboratory panel at screening, W7D1, and EOT may be insufficient",
      "quote": "Autoimmune Laboratory Panell | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Autoimmune panel is only at screening, W7D1, and EOT. Given the immunomodulatory mechanism, more frequent monitoring may be needed to detect immune-related AEs.",
      "fix": "Consider adding autoimmune panel at additional timepoints, such as Q3W visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Long-term survival follow-up phone call only at Q3 months with ±4 weeks window",
      "quote": "Long-Term Survival Follow-up (LTSFU)d (Q3mo) ± 4weeks",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The LTSFU window of ±4 weeks is very wide, which may lead to inconsistent data collection and potential loss to follow-up.",
      "fix": "Tighten the window to ±2 weeks to ensure more consistent follow-up data."
    }
  ]
}
